sourceNote: All records curated from Wikipedia articles and publicly documented sources. Shimla is at 2206m altitude, the former summer capital of British India. Year-round destination; best Oct–Jun, Jul–Aug is monsoon. All records needs_review. NOTE: Kalka–Shimla Railway coordinate intentionally matches destination center — this is the correct coordinate for the railway station in Shimla town.

places.name: The Ridge, Shimla
places.description: A large open promenade running through the heart of Shimla at 2213m, the social and commercial centre of the city. The Ridge connects Christ Church (1857) to the east and the historic Gaiety Theatre to the west. Unobstructed views of the surrounding Himalayan peaks on clear days; covered in snow in winter. The main venue for festivals and public gatherings. No entry fee; open all day. The adjoining Mall Road is Shimla's premier shopping street.

places.name: Jakhu Temple
places.description: Ancient Hanuman temple at the summit of Jakhu Hill, the highest point near Shimla at 2455m. The temple is mentioned in the Ramayana; associated with Hanuman resting here while searching for the Sanjeevani herb. A 33-metre steel Hanuman statue (2010) dominates the hill. Reached via 2km trail from The Ridge (steep, 45 min) or by cable car. Resident rhesus monkeys are numerous and will grab food or belongings. Free entry to the temple; cable car and ropeway charged separately.

places.name: Viceregal Lodge
places.description: Imposing Elizabethan-style stone mansion built 1888, the summer residence of the Viceroy of India during British rule. Several pivotal decisions of the Independence movement were made here, including the Simla Conference of 1945. Now operated as the Indian Institute of Advanced Study; exterior and gardens can be visited on a guided tour, interior on scheduled tours. Declared a heritage building by ASI. Set in large gardens with panoramic Himalayan views.
places.openingDays: Mon–Sat 09:30–17:00 (guided tours; closed Sun and public holidays)

places.name: Mall Road Shimla
places.description: Shimla's main pedestrianised commercial street, running parallel to The Ridge at a lower elevation, stretching roughly 1.8km. Lined with colonial-era buildings housing shops, restaurants, banks, and hotels. The street is motor-vehicle-free; a pleasant evening walk with views downslope into the Shimla hillsides. Handicraft shops sell Himachali shawls, apple products, and local crafts. The original Gaiety Theatre (1887) is at the western end; renovated and in use.

places.name: Kalka–Shimla Railway
places.description: UNESCO World Heritage narrow-gauge railway (762mm) built 1903, running 96km from Kalka (656m) to Shimla (2076m) through 102 tunnels and across 864 bridges. The train climb of 1420m in altitude offers a panoramic view of Himalayan foothills and was engineered by the British to connect the plains to their summer capital. Multiple daily services operated by Indian Railways; the journey takes approximately 5–6 hours. The Shimla terminus is in the lower town at Cart Road.
places.openingDays: Multiple daily services; timetable varies by season

places.name: Christ Church Shimla
places.description: Neo-Gothic Anglican church at the eastern end of The Ridge, completed 1857 — the second oldest church in North India and an iconic symbol of colonial Shimla. Five original stained-glass windows representing Faith, Hope, Charity, Fortitude and Patience were created by Lockwood Kipling (father of Rudyard Kipling). The building is constructed of local stone; the tower is a prominent Shimla landmark. Still holds regular services. Free to enter outside service times.
places.openingDays: Daily 08:00–18:00 (during services access may be restricted)

places.name: Chadwick Falls
places.description: Waterfall dropping 67m through a forested ravine in the Summer Hill area of Shimla, 7km from the town centre. The trail to the falls passes through cedar and rhododendron forest; the waterfall is most dramatic during and after monsoon (Jul–Sep). A government-maintained viewpoint above the falls provides a partial view. Less visited than the main Ridge attractions, making it a genuine alternative for those seeking nature within Shimla's bounds. The approach road and trail are rough.

places.name: Kufri
places.description: Small hill station 16km east of Shimla at 2623m, known for skiing and snow activities in winter (Jan–Mar) and horse riding and Himalayan Nature Park in summer. Kufri has a Himalayan Wildlife Zoo with snow leopard, red panda, and Himalayan birds. The local activity operators organise horse rides to the Mahasu Peak viewpoint (2 km uphill). A half-day excursion from Shimla; shares the same bus route as Chail.

places.name: Tara Devi Temple
places.description: 8th-century temple dedicated to Tara Devi (Goddess Tara) on a hilltop 11km west of Shimla on the National Highway. The main temple building is of Himachali wooden-pagoda style with a newer concrete prayer hall. Considered a Shakti Peeth by local tradition. Good views of the Shimla ridge from the temple hilltop. Reached by a steep flight of approximately 250 steps from the road, or a slightly longer path from the back. Free to visit.

places.name: State Museum Shimla
places.description: Himachal Pradesh State Museum housed in a colonial-era building (1974) below Chaura Maidan, displaying archaeological finds, Pahari miniature paintings, sculptures, textiles, and numismatic collections. The Pahari miniature painting collection is especially notable — covering 17th–19th century miniatures from Kangra, Kullu, Chamba, and Basohli schools. A small but well-curated museum that merits 1–1.5 hours. Entry is nominal. Closed Mondays.
